behavior: The database enforces the money rules: unique receive address and idempotency key, unique transfers, append-only ledger
acceptance: Migrations create users, profiles, profile_wallets, chains, tokens, invoices, chain_transfers, ledger_entries, settlement_intents, chain_cursors and outbox_events; amounts NUMERIC(78,0), addresses text with chain_family

Tests against Postgres: a duplicate (chain_id, receive_address), duplicate (profile_id, idempotency_key), duplicate (chain_id, tx_hash, log_index) while the first is not reorged, an unbalanced ledger transaction, and any UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on the ledger are rejected
notes: 2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Pass. Ran pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test (all ok) and probed a temp PG17 DB. Holds: UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on both ledger tables raise, also via TRUNCATE invoices/chain_transfers/chains/users CASCADE and in replica mode; DELETE of a booked transfer or its invoice fails on FK (no CASCADE); unbalanced txn rejected at commit and with SET CONSTRAINTS IMMEDIATE; composite FKs reject a cross-invoice deposit, a cross-invoice reversal, and a transfer to another invoice's address; partial index allows re-insert after reorged; uint256 bounds and lowercase CHECKs work; Down migration leaves only users. No blocking defects. Non-blocking: (1) 00002_money.sql:116,152 a ledger_transactions row with zero entries commits; it takes the transfer's one-deposit slot (:131), and balanced entries can be added to it later in another DB txn. Fix: deferred constraint trigger on ledger_transactions requiring >=2 entries. (2) A booked transfer can still be set to reorged and its re-mined copy booked again (receiver doubled in probe); only D-45 app logic stops this. Add a guard or an R-21 property check in F049. (3) :109 the same tx live twice at a different log_index (old row not yet marked reorged) is accepted; :100 rejects re-inserting the original block after an A-B-A reorg. F048 must mark rows reorged before inserting and flip rows back rather than re-insert. (4) :191 status failed requires tx_hash, so R-22 'refused, nothing sent' cannot be recorded as failed; adjust in F050. (5) :104 the FK to the invoice token blocks storing Arc native-coin Transfer logs from the 0xffff..fffe emitter that money-safety.md says to index; decide in F048. (6) Invoice terms such as amount can be UPDATEd (receive_address is locked only once transfers exist); the signer recompute (R-22) covers it. (7) :59 bigint expires_at cannot hold uint64 max; fine under the R-19 365-day cap. (8) No test for one-deposit-per-transfer or the deposit/reversal same-invoice FKs; not acceptance lines.

2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: Fail, 1 blocking. BLOCKING: apps/backend/internal/database/migrations/00002_money.sql:267 Down runs DROP FUNCTION chain_transfers_reject_booked_change() while trigger chain_transfers_booked (:215) still exists; chain_transfers is dropped only at :272. Reproduced on PG17 by applying Up then Down: ERROR cannot drop function ... trigger chain_transfers_booked depends on it. Fix: move that DROP FUNCTION below DROP TABLE chain_transfers. No test runs Down, so verify passed. HOLDS (probed): backend tests ok; has_entries rejects an empty txn at commit, also in replica mode; CTE booking passes under SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE; two-statement booking passes when deferred; a single later entry to a committed txn is rejected; an unconfirmed deposit is rejected, also in replica mode; a booked transfer cannot be updated, also in replica mode; booked transfers and invoices cannot be deleted; reversal of a deposit works; reorg-first then booking in READ COMMITTED fails 'not confirmed'; booking under REPEATABLE READ against a concurrent reorg gets a serialization error. NON-BLOCKING: (a) :175-185 the race guard holds only when the reorg UPDATE runs in READ COMMITTED. With booking committed first and the reorg in REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE (snapshot taken before the booking commits), the UPDATE waits, then succeeds because a FOR SHARE lock is not a write and the trigger's EXISTS uses the old snapshot. Probe result: transfer reorged AND booked. pgx defaults to READ COMMITTED, so this is fine today; state it in architecture.md and F048, or have the booking write the transfer row. (b) A reversed deposit's transfer still cannot change (correct under D-45). (c) Earlier notes 3-8 are unchanged.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Pass. Previous blocking finding fixed: Down now drops chain_transfers_reject_booked_change() after chain_transfers (00002_money.sql:281); Up-Down-Up runs cleanly in psql and through goose (migrations_down_test.go). Backend tests ok; the 4 new tests passed 5 of 5 runs (-count=5). Race guard (booked flag, :174-203) probed with booking-first and reorg-first across RC/RR/SERIALIZABLE on both sides (17 cases): every case ends with one side rejected (P0001 in RC, 40001 otherwise); 0 transfers end up reorged and booked. Replica mode: direct booked=true and unbooking both rejected. A failed (unbalanced) deposit and a rollback to a savepoint both reset booked. Booked transfers can't be re-booked after a reversal. NON-BLOCKING: (1) 'booked only by a ledger deposit' (:99) holds for UPDATE only. Three probe paths leave booked=true with no deposit: INSERT INTO chain_transfers (...booked) VALUES (...true) (the trigger at :223 is BEFORE UPDATE only); INSERT INTO ledger_transactions ... OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE with a colliding id ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (the BEFORE trigger's UPDATE survives the skipped row); and a temp-table trigger that runs the UPDATE at pg_trigger_depth 2 (TEMP is granted to PUBLIC by default). Result: the transfer can never be booked or changed (under-count, owner fix needed), never a double count. Fix: one deferred constraint trigger on chain_transfers checking booked = EXISTS(deposit) at commit, which would also make the pg_trigger_depth check unnecessary; or at least fire :223 on INSERT too. (2) An idempotent booking with ON CONFLICT (chain_transfer_id) DO NOTHING raises P0001 instead of doing nothing; F049 must expect that. (3) Deposit entries are not tied to chain_transfers.amount, and a reversed deposit's transfer can never be booked again, so a wrong-amount deposit cannot be corrected by re-booking. Enforce entry = transfer amount in F049. (4) Earlier notes 6-8 still apply.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: Pass. Note 1 fixed: the deferred constraint trigger chain_transfers_booked_matches_ledger (00002_money.sql:203-210, :235) rejects at commit all three earlier paths: a direct INSERT with booked=true, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE, and the temp-table trigger. It also rejects booked=true set in replica mode. After the probes, 0 transfers have booked out of line with the ledger. Normal booking (one statement or two) passes at RC, RR and SERIALIZABLE; reversal works; the watcher's status updates on unbooked transfers work. Booking-first and reorg-first races at all 9 isolation pairs (18 cases) each end with one side rejected (P0001 or 40001); 0 transfers are reorged and booked. Two concurrent deposits for one transfer: the second is rejected. Down: Up then Down leaves only users, with 0 functions; goose TestMigrationsRollBackAndReapply ok. Backend tests ok; the ledger, booking and rollback tests passed 5 of 5 runs (-count=5). NON-BLOCKING: (1) :208 when the transfer row is deleted in the same transaction (insert-then-delete, or update-then-delete of an unbooked row), the subquery returns NULL, NULL IS DISTINCT FROM false is true, and the commit is rejected. No planned flow deletes transfers. Fix if needed: skip when the row is gone. (2) Under SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE a normal booking now fails: the nested UPDATE's check fires before the ledger row exists. The app uses the deferred default, so this is fine; do not use IMMEDIATE when booking. (3) Earlier notes 7-8 still apply; notes 2, 3 and 6 are now on F049.
